caption: I budgeted R1 500 for nappies and formula. It's R2 800 and she's not even on solids yet. What did nobody warn you about?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R33 500
p/m salary
Living in Pietermaritzburg
slides.body:
Male, 33
Married, one baby (3 months)
Job: Warehouse supervisor
Net salary: R33 500 p/m

slides.title: Bond
slides.body: We bought before she was pregnant. Good timing we didn't plan for.

slides.title: Baby costs
slides.includes: Nappies, formula top-ups, clinic visits, the clothes she's already grown out of
slides.body: I budgeted R1 500 for this. It's R2 800, and she's not even on solids yet.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: The one thing on this list that hasn't changed since the baby.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Big monthly shop plus the pharmacy runs that never used to happen
slides.body: It's still two adults eating, but somehow the trolley is fuller every time.

slides.title: Medical aid
slides.includes: Family plan, upgraded the week we found out
slides.body: Worth every rand at 2am with a screaming three month old. I still felt the jump on the payslip.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Petrol & insurance, electricity & water, phone & fibre, funeral policy, stokvel, new life cover, black tax
slides.body: R9 000 of things that all quietly grew the month she arrived.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R33 500. She's on unpaid leave until October, so this is the whole household running on one salary for now.

slides.title: I stopped guessing what the baby cost
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

The baby line alone had grown by R1 300 in eight weeks, and I hadn't noticed until I saw it in one place.

No bank login needed.
